name: John Maynard Keynes
kicker: British economist · Said governments should spend to fight recessions
briefing: When the world’s economies collapsed during the Great Depression, John Maynard Keynes argued for a bold, controversial fix: have governments spend their way out of trouble. This British economist had already made headlines by predicting that harsh peace terms after World War I would backfire. His 1936 book _The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money_ reshaped how governments fight recessions to this day.

tossups.p: This man once used the example of carrying an umbrella in case of rain to discuss chance and belief in _A Treatise on Probability_. He resigned from the British Treasury after hardliners nicknamed the “Heavenly Twins” pushed for harsh war reparations at the Paris Peace Conference.
tossups.r: This thinker then criticized those reparations as a “Carthaginian peace” in _The Economic Consequences of the Peace_. He later argued that governments should spend more, even running deficits, to fight recessions and unemployment. For 10 points, name this British economist who wrote _The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money_.

tossups.p: This thinker criticized the gold standard and argued that some inflation was better than painful deflation in _A Tract on Monetary Reform_, where he also joked, “In the long run we are all dead.” He later argued that wages and prices are “sticky,” meaning they adjust only slowly to changing markets.
tossups.r: This economist rejected the classical idea called Say’s Law, that supply always creates its own demand. He claimed that aggregate demand, not aggregate supply, drives total output and employment. For 10 points, name this British economist who advocated government spending to fight recessions.

tossups.p: This thinker introduced “liquidity preference,” the idea that people’s demand for cash depends on interest rates. Economist John Hicks later summarized this man’s ideas in a graph called the IS-LM model, while this thinker’s own namesake “cross” plots aggregate demand against national income.
tossups.r: This man criticized the harsh reparations placed on Germany in _The Economic Consequences of the Peace_. He argued that governments should spend more during downturns to fight unemployment. For 10 points, name this British economist, the author of _The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money_.

tossups.p: During World War II, this man proposed higher taxes and compulsory saving to help pay for Britain’s war effort. He later led the British delegation at the Bretton Woods [“BREH-tun woodz”] Conference, where he proposed an international currency called the bancor and helped plan what became the World Bank.
tossups.r: This thinker was made a Baron in 1942 and took a seat in Britain’s House of Lords. His ideas sparked a “Keynesian Revolution” toward demand-focused economics. For 10 points, name this British economist who advocated government spending to combat recessions.

tossups.p: A member of the artistic Bloomsbury [“BLOOMZ-ber-ee”] Group, this man married the Russian ballerina Lydia Lopokova [“loh-puh-KOH-vuh”] in 1925. Years earlier, hardliners nicknamed the “Heavenly Twins” had excluded him from key reparations talks at the Paris Peace Conference.
tossups.r: This thinker then wrote _The Economic Consequences of the Peace_, warning that harsh terms on Germany would backfire. He argued that aggregate demand, not aggregate supply, drives employment and output. For 10 points, name this British economist who advocated deficit spending to fight recessions, the author of _The General Theory_.

tossups.p: This thinker compared the stock market to a newspaper contest where readers guess which photo everyone else will pick, a “beauty contest” analogy for investor behavior. His namesake “Cross” graphs aggregate demand against national income to find economic equilibrium.

trap.title: Keynes, Hicks, or Hayek?
trap.body: Clues about Keynes often name other economists in the same breath: John Hicks, who turned Keynes’s ideas into the IS-LM graph, and Friedrich Hayek and Milton Friedman, who argued against government spending and are usually paired against Keynes in class. Keynes’s own father, John Neville Keynes, was also a Cambridge economist and shares the last name.
trap.fix: If the clue says a graph is “named after” or “summarized” this economist’s ideas by someone else, or contrasts “this economist” with a rival school of thought, the answer is still Keynes, not the other name in the sentence.
